source.title: From P systems to morphogenetic systems: an overview and open problems

accepted.question_text: Define a notion of descriptional complexity for a morphogenetic system (M system), a computational model in Euclidean space built from floating objects, tiles, protions, and reaction rules, and then construct a computationally universal M system that is minimal with respect to that complexity measure. In doing so, determine whether the smallest universal system can simulate Turing machines with only polynomial slowdown or whether exponential slowdown is unavoidable.

evidence.quote: Open Problem 1 Minimal universal M system: define a descriptional complexity of an M system. Try to construct a minimal M system which is computationally universal, eventually distinguishing polynomial/exponential slowdown compared to the Turing machine.

accepted.question_text: Consider Monte Carlo M systems, meaning probabilistic morphogenetic systems that accept an instance if a distinguished floating object yes appears within polynomially many steps with probability at least 1/2 and reject if yes never appears. What is the exact computational complexity class of decision problems solvable by such systems in polynomial time in the semi-uniform sense? In particular, does this class include PSPACE?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 2 What is the exact characterization of the class of problems solvable in this way by Monte Carlo M systems in polynomial time? Does it, for instance, contain also the class PSPACE?

accepted.question_text: How does the computational efficiency of morphogenetic systems change if one imposes the recognizer-style requirement that the system must halt, in the sense that from some point onward no rule is applicable, and that exactly one distinguished output object, yes or no, is released only at the final computation step?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 3 How would the computational efficiency of M systems change if we insisted on halting (in the sense that no rule is applicable from a certain moment on) and releasing the object yes or no at the last step of computation?

accepted.question_text: Do there exist morphogenetic systems that are computationally universal in the Turing sense and at the same time self-healing for injuries of degree strictly greater than 1, where the degree of an injury is the graph-theoretic distance between the pre-injury and post-injury configurations in the configuration digraph?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 4 Are there Turing-universal M systems which are simultaneously self-healing of a degree greater than 1?

Definition 6 [18] An injury to a morphogenetic system M is a transition of the system given by a pair of configurations (x, y) such that y cannot be obtained from x by any one step of the system M. The degree of the injury is the undirected graph-theoretic distance between x and y in the configuration digraph.

accepted.question_text: Investigate self-replicating morphogenetic systems that achieve the best possible self-healing degree. Equivalently, determine how robust a self-replicating M system can be against injuries while still preserving self-healing in the formal sense defined for the model.

evidence.quote: Open Problem 5 Investigate self-replicating M systems which are self-healing of a best possible degree.

accepted.question_text: Model viruses as geometrically simple agents inside a population of cells represented by a morphogenetic system, and use the model to simulate and analyze how viral infection spreads through that cell population. Develop the model so that its predictions are meaningful at the level of macro-observables rather than only at the level of microscopic simulation details.
accepted.context_brief: Virus spread in M-system cell populations

evidence.quote: Open Problem 6 Viruses are objects with a simple geometry and behavior. Simulate and study spreading of viruses in a cell population, try to make the model relevant at the level of macro-observables.
